member.summary: Class to construct and return JSON objects

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.Balance.JsonConstructer.Construct(System.Object[])
member.summary:
Constructs and returns a JSON object based on the parameters of nested arrays.
This method will take an array of objects in the format [obj1, obj2, obj3, obj4] and convert them to a JSON object of the form { "obj1": "obj2", "obj3":"obj4" }. If the object in the postParams array is an array itself it will try to nest the object in the json. For example, if obj2 is an array consisting of [a,b], the result will be: { "obj1": { "a", "b" }, "obj3":"obj4" }.
If the object is an actual array it must be a string starting with "[". For example, if obj2 is a string like this "[a,b]", the result will be: { "obj1": [a,b], "obj3":"obj4" }.
TODO: Remove this method replace with built in Json serialization

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.Balance.SharedObjects.BalanceReplaceKitResponseModel
member.summary:
The information returned from Balance after a kit replacement
There are 3 ways that this can come back: 1) Balance Successfully replaces the kits: CurrentItemNumbers = null Errors = null SuccessfulResponse will be an object with all properties filled in, except for subject which is filled in on our side.
2) Specific Kit mismatch balance error: CurrentItemNumbers = some array of new item numbers to replace ours with Errors = that specific balance error SuccessfulResponse = null
3) Any other error: CurrentItemNumbers = null Errors = that returned balance error SuccessfulResponse = null

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsInternalAllowed
member.summary: Returns true if internal endpoints are allowed to run like normal endpoints. They will still be logged. NOTE: Internal endpoints should basically never go through validation, since swapping means we don't need to validate. We should only see logs if we run our swappers through validation to test the validity of our swappers.

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsUnsupportedAllowed
member.summary: Returns true if unsupported endpoints are allowed to run like normal endpoints. They will still be logged.

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsAnalyzeDatabaseSwaps
member.summary: Returns true if we analyze custom functions that were swapped in the database. Returns false if we do not analyze custom functions that were swapped in the database. This is useful if we need to add a custom function to the database for a client that would otherwise violate the whitelist. If we need to turn this off, we should add the endpoint which violated the whitelist as an endpoint in the following release. If we do not want to make that endpoint available to clients it can be marked as "SupportedWhitelist.Internal".

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsAnalyzeBeforeEvalAtRuntime
member.summary: Returns true if we analyze custom functions for access whitelist issues prior to running them at runtime. Returns false if we execute custom functions at runtime without checking them for whitelist compatibility first. If you want to also prevent them from running use CustomFunctionIsFailedAnalysisAllowedToRun tag.

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsFailedAnalysisAllowedToRun
member.summary: Returns true if we allow failed custom function scans to be ran. If this is false, custom functions that fail analysis (I.E. ones not on the whitelist) can still run. If we want to stop unsupported custom function endpoints from running: CustomFunctionIsAnalyzeBeforeEvalAtRuntime must be true. CustomFunctionIsUnsupportedAllowed must be false. CustomFunctionIsFailedAnalysisAllowedToRun must be false.

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsEndpointUsageLogged
member.summary: Returns true if we log Unsupported or FullOnly whitelist usages.

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.DefaultCustomerApiCompatibilityVersion
member.summary: Returns CustomerApi version which is used by default (int).

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.DefaultLegacyCustomerApiCompatibilityVersion
member.summary: Returns maximum CustomerApi version which will not throw errors by default (int).

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsDotNetUnsupportedAllowed
member.summary: Returns true if dot net unsupported endpoints are allowed to run like normal endpoints. They will still be logged.

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsUsingSwappers
member.summary: Returns true if swappers are enabled for custom functions. Swappers change certain custom functions to instead use internal implementations.

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionUseSharedApiOnly
member.summary: Returns true if IsClassic studies are restricted to Shared Apis only. They will still be logged.

member.name: F:Medidata.Core.Objects.ConfigTags.CustomFunctionIsDatabaseSwapEnabled
member.summary: Returns true if custom function code swaps can be loaded from the database. Database swaps exist to allow us to CMP clients who have bad functionality in the C# swappers. Developers should NOT be using this to change client custom functions unless in case of emergency. Instead create a C# implementation as a Precompiled custom function or a swapper.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.CRFMigrator.MigrationExecution.RunHasLockedStudySiteSubjects(System.Int32)
member.summary: Returns true if the specified migration run has any subject whose study site is currently locked. Used by the migration UI to display banner warnings on Migration Results / Migration Details when the delete-dry-run / restore-subject actions are not available.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.CRFMigrator.MigrationExecution.DryRunHasLockedSourceStudySiteSubjects(System.Int32)
member.summary: Returns true if any of the Dry Run migration run's SOURCE subjects (the original production/aux subjects referenced via MigrationSubjectList.SourceSubjectID) are currently in a locked study site. Unlike , which checks the Dry Run's own copied subjects (MigrationSubjectList.SubjectID) living in the Dry Run/target environment, this checks the original subjects that "Execute Migration" will operate on at runtime. It mirrors the scheduler's runtime lock check in MigrationTaskCallbacks.PerformMigration, which fetches the Execution's MigrationSubjectList.SubjectID (populated from the Dry Run's SourceSubjectID by spMigrationCopyDryRunSubjectsToExecute) and inspects that subject's StudySite.IsLocked.
member.param: The Dry Run migration run id.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.CRFMigrator.MigrationExecution.CRFVersionHasLockedStudySiteSubjects(System.Int32)
member.summary: Returns true if any active, non-deleted subject on the given CRF version is in a locked study site. Used by the Quick Publish (Publish Checks) UI to hide the Publish/Schedule buttons and show a banner, and as a stale-page guard before a publish-in-place run is created. This mirrors the locked study site check enforced by spMigrationInPlaceSubjectsInsert.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.Definitions.DerivationDefinition
member.summary:
The Derivation object represents the calculation of a derived value for a DataPoint. Derived DataPoints are those whose value is the result of a calculation involving other DataPoints ( Age = DateEnrolledInStudy - DateOfBirth ). The Field and the Folder objects are filters that restrict this Derivation to those Variables that appear in the specified Field or Folder.
This object cannot be created directly. Instead one must go through the Derivations collection to create Derivation objects.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.Definitions.DerivationStepDefinition
member.summary:
The DerivationStep represents a step in the calculation of a derived value for a DataPoint. Derived DataPoints are those whose value is the result of a calculation involving other DataPoints ( Age = DateEnrolledInStudy - DateOfBirth ). The Field and the Folder objects are filters that restrict this step in the Derivation to those Variables that appear in the specified Field or Folder.
This object cannot be created directly. Instead one must use the Derivation object to create a DerivationSteps collection.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.Derivation
member.summary:
The Derivation object represents the calculation of a derived value for a DataPoint. Derived DataPoints are those whose value is the result of a calculation involving other DataPoints ( Age = DateEnrolledInStudy - DateOfBirth ). The Field and the Folder objects are filters that restrict this Derivation to those Variables that appear in the specified Field or Folder.
This object cannot be created directly. Instead one must go through the Derivations collection to create Derivation objects.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.DerivationStep
member.summary:
The DerivationStep represents a step in the calculation of a derived value for a DataPoint. Derived DataPoints are those whose value is the result of a calculation involving other DataPoints ( Age = DateEnrolledInStudy - DateOfBirth ). The Field and the Folder objects are filters that restrict this step in the Derivation to those Variables that appear in the specified Field or Folder.
This object cannot be created directly. Instead one must use the Derivation object to create a DerivationSteps collection.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.ObjectiveReference
member.summary: An objective reference is the fundamental reference in the Library object definition hierarchy. It implies that the target of the reference takes part in the source object's definition. If the source is taken out of its LibraryVersion context, the target object has to come along if the source is to still be functionally defined. In a great majority of cases, an objective reference is recognizable by its mirroring of a database model dependency (see Literal/Logical references below). There are exceptions, the objects that do not inherit PrimaryLibraryObject: CheckSteps, DerivationSteps and CheckActions. In those cases, we define an objective reference as from a check to its steps etc, because functionally -- if not purely in terms of data -- a check is useless without its steps and actions, and the same is true for derivations. Objective references are always unidirectional, which is guaranteed by the integrity of the object/database model. The object layer, of course, provides bi-directional references as a utility, but -- without exception -- only one of the directions, if any, constitutes an objective reference. Currently, for instance, a data dictionary physically references no other object (except for the version itself), and yet you can get the property Entries; but in that case, the system in fact searches through the Entries table or cache in order to find the ones with an objective reference back to the dictionary. There are also "soft" references, which are defined as references that are allowed to break upon the extraction of the source from its Library Version context. The source is then not considered undefined, but merely "incomplete" -- but, use it however it suits your purposes. Another classification is "mandatory" vs. "optional" references. Mandatory objective references target objects of a type that would inevitably accompany ANY object of the source object's type (Field->Form, Entry->Dictionary are examples), while objects targeted by Optional objective references must accompany THE PARTICULAR source object, but not any object of the same type (for example, Variable->Derivation or Folder->(Parent)Folder). An object with an unfulfilled mandatory objective reference cannot be committed to the database, while if optional references are unfulfilled the object can still be committed (though, again, its definition will not be complete; this is useful for temporary committs). There are, as of now, two Objective Reference models: Logical and literal. The literal model exactly mirrors the database model. The logical model represents how we THINK about these objects and how they function. The differences between the two are the opposite directions of objective references between a check and its steps, a check and its actions and a derivation and its steps. Logical model incorporates a Parent->Children reference in these cases, while the Literal mode includes Child->Parent relationships. In other words, a check is functionally useless without its steps; but when saving to the database, the opposite is true: you can save a stepless check, but not a checkless step.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.ObjectiveReferenceCluster
member.summary: An ObjectiveReferenceCluster is a tree-like structure of ObjectiveReferenceNodes, which can each have one parent and multiple branches. A cluster is "seeded" with a LibraryObject, which then forms the cluster root node and propagates to create new nodes populated with its objective reference targets. Then each of them does the same, and so on recursively. Seeding an ObjectiveReferenceCluster will give you a structure with objects that would, only together, constitute the entire LibraryVersion-context independent definition of the seeding object. A cluster can also be formed against a "target" LibraryVersion, if the intent of cluster creation is to copy an object to another known LibraryVersion. In the future, equivalency context will be variant -- so you'll be able to seed a field cluster against a certain form etc. This can help resolve identity conflicts like duplicate OIDs and such. Any objects in nodes whose path to root includes a soft objective reference are considered softly referenced. Lastly, you can build reverse clusters, that are seeded with referenced objects and branch to referencing objects. They answer the question "what all references this object?".

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.ObjectiveReferenceMolecule
member.summary: A many-to-many interconnected structure of ObjectiveReferenceAtoms, which each contain a LibraryObject. Unlike is the case of ObjectiveReferenceCluster, objects in ObjectiveReferenceAtoms are unique within an ObjectiveReferenceMolecule. Therefore, as a structure to represent a LibraryVersion-context free definition of multiple objects, it is much more efficient than multiple ObjectiveReferenceClusters. It is not "seeded" like an ObjectiveReferenceCluster, and you can add objects to it freely after creating an ObjectiveReferenceMolecule. Another functional distinction from an ObjectiveReferenceCluster is that it provides an opportunity to get objective-reference sources of references to a given object (among the objects added) -- and not only the down-river dependencies. As new objects are added, an interdependent structure forms -- or several of them -- floating free from any LibraryVersion, or any other, context. Once you are done adding objects, you can pass an object to Fuse() the ObjectiveReferenceMolecule, which will then form a central ObjectiveReferenceAtom with the object you passed in the constructor, and be the target of references from all ObjectiveReferenceAtoms which until that time had no outgoing references. You must Fuse() to an object that has no outgoing objective references. When you fuse, references to objects within the ObjectiveReferenceMolecule that are of the same library object type will be re-routed to the new, central atom. For example, if you fuse a bunch of fields to a form, any form references they had will be re-routed to the central ObjectiveReferenceAtom. At that point, you'll have a singular structure, and you're able to do a save operation which starts from the center -- the target object, conceptually speaking -- and goes outward, saving objects in the order of inverse objective-reference dependencies, passing their new IDs to the objects that depend on them along the way , after which they are marked as belonging to the target. An object is saved -- and its ObjectiveReferenceAtom marked as in target context -- only when the ObjectiveReferenceAtom has no outgoing references to source context atoms left. In some cases, there can be indirectly circular objective references, in which case you can be left with one or more ring-like structures of objects, which are then saved with multiple passes. The integrity of the object model, and consequently ObjectiveReference definitions, ensures that circular-reference rings contain at least one reference that is not mandatory. Non-mandatory references are references to objects that must be there to define THAT PARTICULAR object, but not any object of that type. This means that a partial multiple-pass save of an objective-reference ring (the ring-breaker element gets saved and later updated) is always possible; once an optional reference is found, the ring can be broken and becomes linear, easy to save in the inverse reference direction. In the future, object equivalency context will be variant. For now, we're assuming fusing to LibraryVersions. ///// You can also use ObjectiveReferenceMolecule as a cluster-buffer. You can add already-made clusters to it, and you can seed clusters with atoms -- in effect "peel" clusters from molecules.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.ObjectiveReferenceNode
member.summary: An ObjectiveReferenceNode at its heart has a LibraryObject. It is the basic unit of an ObjectiveReferenceCluster. It can have only a single parent, and multiple branches. member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.ObjectiveReferenceParticle
member.summary: An ObjectiveReferenceParticle is like an ObjectiveReferenceAtom but stripped down to only containing an object and a reference to a parent atom, the incoming reference. It is used as a placeholder when building an ObjectiveReferenceMolecule, which does not automatically add atoms that result from an object's cluster's soft references -- since those, by definition, do not imply a relationship necessary for the source's definition. Instead, an ObjectiveReferenceParticle containing an object which is the target of the relevant soft reference will be created, with a reference to the atom containing the object soft referencing the particle's object. If that object is explicitly added to the ObjectiveReferenceMolecule later, a real atom containing it will replace the particle and all relationships will be properly formed. If it is not and the molecule is fused and saved, the relevant property that links the atom's object with the particle's will be updated and set to null. More specifically, this way we can, for example, add a field that references a variable that soft-references the derivation. If the molecule is fused and saved afterwards, the variable's derivation reference will be removed. If the derivation is added before the fusing, it will take its rightful place as a reference target of the variable.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.ObjectiveReferenceTable
member.summary: There is no sure-fire way to reliably determine whether a reference between Library objects is objective or not (see ObjectiveReference.cs) by using Reflection or parsing the database, because the nature of an object relationship also depends on human object interpretation and not only on their raw structure. This is where we statically store definitions of the objective references enforced in our current object model. Two hashtables are maintained -- Literal and Logical. Literal references are those strictly following the object model, and Logical following our logical conception of objects. They are very similar. This class cannot be inherited.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.OmniLoader.API.Client
member.summary: Use this class as a static way to communicate with the client. Behind the curtains it is really only the thread-static StatusOrderedHash object, s_statusHash. As you're manipulating it, you ocassionally save it to the database by calling Update(). The client is a CtlUpload, and is doing Ajax queries of the database every so often (how often is governed by CtlUpload.UpdateCyclePeriod). This all creates the effect of nearly seamless writing onto the client's screen. For example: you want the log window to display a message? Call Client.SetLogLine(blah). Progress bar to 50%? Client.Progress = 50. When you want it displayed on the client, you call Client.Update() (but if you're in a loop, look into using ManageProgress(), which will call Client.Update() for you). Live logging must be initialized with Client.StartLiveLogging() first. If it isn't, loader will operate in "scheduled" mode, and only save its status at the very end. It's important to note that s_statusHash is also accessible from the web threads. This class cannot be inherited.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.OmniLoader.API.UploadThreadBase.RunThread
member.summary: User implementation of the upload thread. At this point, you already have automatic access to the uploaded workbook and user interaction (m_workbook and m_interaction, in class scope), and thread-static connection, transaction, and localization (UI and workbook) with UploadContext. You also have access to the client status hash. You don't need to worry about handling transaction commit or rollback -- OmniLoader will figure out what to do based on the status data you set.

member.name: T:Medidata.Core.Objects.PostMarket.GridColumn
member.summary:
GridColumn class is used to define a patient dashboard data grid column.
The patient data grid consists of rows of subject data which is subdivided into columns. Each row column coordinate references a grid cell which will contain information about the subject.
Column attributes are: ID - the id of the column ProjectID - Id of project associated with this column. Ordinal - the ordinal position of the column within the datagrid layout ColName - the name of the column which is used to reference it's data values IsVisible - indicates if the column is visible in the datagrid IsSortable - indicates if the column can be sorted by the user IsUserConfigurable - indicates if the user can modify the column using the builder

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.Programmability.PrecompiledFunctions.BalanceRandomizeFunctionService.Evaluate(System.Object)
member.summary: Request that this subject be randomized in Balance through web service call. Sends fields qualified in edit check to Balance, the study.ExternalID, site.ExternalID, and subject.NumberInStudy. Balance will match fields to strata factors by field.Name. On success, target DataPoint gets success comment, and fields with OIDs such as REGIME_NAME, REGIME_RATIO, REGIME_DESCRIPTION, RANDOMIZED_AT, STRATUM_NAME, STRATUM_CAP, and REGIME_SELECTION_METHOD will be populated with data about the subject from Balance. On error, queries with appropriate messages will be placed on the target DataPoint.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.Programmability.PrecompiledFunctions.RsgCaseIdAndFolder1FunctionService.Evaluate(System.Object)
member.summary: Create a dynamic search list which generates a unique 'CaseID' when 'new' is selected and adds that 'caseID' to the dynamic search list for that subject. When AESER = Yes for the first time in the subject, allow the dynamic search list in field SAEID to have 'new'. When SAEID in forms (AEG001 or AEG002 or AEG003) have 'new' selected generate the 'CaseID' in the following format: <Studyname>_<SubjectName>_<Incremental number per case per subject> (4 digit incremental number)e.g. 'eSAE Study 1_1112222_0001'. When 'new' is selected add the matrices 'eSAE' and update the folder name for folder 'eSAE', with the caseID.
member.returns: Returns null after completing the action.

Only below cases are supported.

var codeId = 2 + 10; // NG var codeId = dp.Version + dp.SecondaryVersion; // NG

member.summary: This class is used to fetch subjects or children of subjects when we need to check the cache to see if the object (or objects) has already been loaded, and whether or not we need to run a status rollup on the subject (or parent subject) in the case that the subject is enqueued for a deferred rollup.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.Repositories.Fetchers.StatusObjectFetcher`3.FindOrCreate(System.Int32,System.Func{`0},Medidata.Interfaces.IInteraction,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Fetches the requested status object from the cache if it exists, otherwise a new object is created. If a new object needs to be created, and its status is out of date (based on the data fetched from the database), a status rollup will be executed and the data will be refetched from the database. If there is no status data available for the status object, a status rollup will be forced, and the data will be refetched from the database.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.Repositories.Fetchers.StatusObjectFetcher`3.FindOrCreate(System.Func{`0},System.Func{`1},Medidata.Interfaces.IInteraction,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Fetches the requested status object from the provided cache if it exists, otherwise a new object is created. If a new object needs to be created, and its status is out of date (based on the data fetched from the database), a status rollup will be executed and the data will be refetched from the database. The DTO provided by will be used to determine which status object is being requested. If there is no status data available for the status object, a status rollup will be forced, and the data will be refetched from the database.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.Repositories.Fetchers.StatusObjectFetcher`3.FindOrCreate(System.Func{System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{`0}},Medidata.Interfaces.IInteraction,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Fetches the requested status objects, based on the DTOs provided by . If any of the requested data objects exist in the cache, they will be retrieved from there. New objects will be created for those DTOs that do not have a corresponding object in the cache. If any of the requested objects is uncached and has out of date status, a status rollup will be executed and the data will be refetched from the database.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.Subject.GetDataPointsByOIDPath(Medidata.Core.Objects.OIDPath)
member.summary: Returns a collection of all the DataPoint objects for the Subject that matches the supplied OIDPath.
member.remarks: If folder and form OIDs are null they are treated as wildcards. This method only returns the presentable DataPoints, i.e. those that aren't log fields on record position zero, or non-fog fields on record position greater than zero. In some conditions this may not return DataPoints being created by the current operation.
member.returns: Collection of DataPoint objects that matches the specified OIDPath.

member.name: M:Medidata.Core.Objects.Subject.Medidata#Interfaces#Clinical#ISubject#GetDataPointsByOidPath(Medidata.Interfaces.Clinical.IOIDPath)
member.summary: Returns all the DataPoints for the Subject that match the supplied OIDPath. If Folder and form OIDs are null they are treated as wildcards. It fetches matching Subject DataPoints directly from the Database and then appends in-memory DataPoints (if any), that are not already saved in the Database, as part of the current operation. This method only returns the presentable DataPoints, i.e. those that aren't Log fields on Recordposition zero, or non-Log Fields on Recordposition greater than zero.
member.returns: Collection of DataPoints that match the specified OIDPath
